sections.heading: Preventative Maintenance, Repair, or a New Roof?

runs.v: How to repair a commercial flat roof? Locate the entry, match the repair to the membrane, and water-test it, as the process above shows. Preventive maintenance schedules should be established for commercial roofs: regular roof inspections at least twice a year help identify potential roof issues early, routine maintenance catches small defects and roofing issues before they escalate, and repairing localized membrane damage prevents larger problems. Proper sealing and maintenance extend the life of roofing systems. Debris can obstruct rooftop drains, so maintaining gutters and drains prevents water accumulation; proper drainage is critical to prevent ponding, because standing water accelerates membrane deterioration and structural sagging can lead to water pooling on flat roofs.

What is the 25% rule in roofing? In New Jersey, repairing more than 25% of a commercial roof in 12 months triggers a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and damage past about 25 to 30% of the roof usually makes a new roof the better investment. An honest assessment of each West Orange roofing project weighs remaining membrane life against repair cost: a membrane that has served West Orange winters for 15 years over wet insulation needs roof replacement for long-lasting protection, while a sound one needs only a fix at the failed seam.
